name: Shao Hongzhi
current_role: Chairman, CEO and actual controller, Nanjing Sunlord Electronics Corp. (商络电子, SZSE: 300975)
profile: Sha Hongzhi (沙宏志; listed by Hurun as 'Shao Hongzhi', company 'Sunlux') founded Nanjing Sunlord Electronics in August 1999 and is its legal representative and actual controller. Sunlord is one of China's leading domestic distributors of passive electronic components (60+ agency lines, 2,000+ customers); it listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Sunlord runs large bonded warehouse/logistics hubs in Nanjing, Shenzhen and Hong Kong with WMS and automatic labelling, plus subsidiaries in Singapore and Taiwan and offices in Thailand and Malaysia.
deep_cut_fact: Before its 2021 ChiNext IPO, Sunlord was first quoted on China's NEEQ 'New Third Board' in 2015; Sha holds an MBA from CEIBS.
notes: Correct Chinese name is 沙宏志 (Sha Hongzhi); Hurun's 'Sunlux' = Nanjing Sunlord Electronics (not Shenzhen Sunlord 002138). CEIBS MBA per MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/HONG-ZHI-SHA-A37YJ1/experience/). Best route: IR email / board secretary.

name: Shou Bonian
current_role: Retired co-founder of Greentown China (former CEO and executive vice chairman); no current executive role found
profile: Shou Bainian (寿柏年, b. 1954) co-founded Hangzhou developer Greentown with Song Weiping, joining in 1998 and serving as executive vice chairman and CEO through the 2006 HK listing and CCCG's 2015 entry. He stepped down as CEO in 2015 and in 2018 sold his entire 8.1% stake (~US$269m) and retired from the board.
interesting_fact: In January 2018 he sold all 174.5m Greentown shares at HK$12.08 each (about US$269m), ending a near-20-year partnership with co-founder Song Weiping.
deep_cut_fact: A history graduate of Hangzhou University (1982), he spent 16 years in government and state roles - Yin County government office, Ningbo municipal general office and China Huaneng's Zhejiang subsidiary - before joining Greentown in April 1998.
notes: Name usually romanized Shou Bainian. Retired and low-profile since 2018; held shares via Profitwise Limited. No published personal contact; Greentown IR is not his office. Alive status inferred from continued Hurun listing (2026) and no death reports.

name: Rostam Abdulrasul Aziz
current_role: Chairman, Taifa Group (Taifa Gas LPG); investor in MIC Tanzania (Tigo/Zantel) and majority owner of Nation Media Group
profile: Tanzanian businessman and former CCM MP for Igunga (1994-2011). Built wealth via a ~35% stake in Vodacom Tanzania (sold 2014-2019 for ~US$470m), Caspian contract mining, and Taifa Gas, East Africa's leading LPG supplier. With Axian he bought Millicom's Tanzanian telecoms, and in 2026 bought 54% of Nation Media Group from the Aga Khan network.
interesting_fact: Forbes called him Tanzania's first dollar billionaire, and Henley & Partners' 2022 Africa Wealth Report named him East Africa's only dollar billionaire.
deep_cut_fact: As Igunga MP in 1996 he started a local health insurance scheme covering a family of four children for about TSh10,000 a year; ex-President Mkapa's memoir credits it as the inspiration for Tanzania's National Health Insurance Fund (2001).
notes: Strong energy angle: Taifa Gas is building LPG import terminals (Dar es Salaam Kigamboni, Mombasa, expanding into Kenya/Zambia). Email is Taifa Gas's general corporate address, not personal. Economics degree from Exeter (UK).

name: Gao Jianrong
current_role: Chairman / actual controller, Tibet Zhongyin Group (西藏中茵集团, 'Join In'), a Suzhou-based property and investment group
profile: Gao Jianrong (高建荣) controls the Zhongyin ('Join In') group with his wife Feng Feifei, who holds 40% of the group. Zhongyin built a Suzhou-area real estate business and around 2007-08 took over listed shell S*ST Tianhua, renamed Zhongyin Co. (600745), which in 2015-16 swapped out property assets for Wingtech's phone ODM business.
interesting_fact: The listed company Zhongyin took control of around 2008 (S*ST Tianhua, later Zhongyin Co.) is today Wingtech Technology, one of China's largest smartphone ODMs and owner of chipmaker Nexperia.
notes: Hurun 'Joinin' = 中茵 Zhongyin/Join In. Very low public profile; little biographical info online (ChinaVitae reportedly lists him as born 1963 in Zhejiang, but I could not open the page to verify). No published contacts found. 2012 filing showing the stake transfer to his wife: https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2012-02/29/A39/AGG0390229C.pdf

name: Wang Chunchan
current_role: Legal representative, Guangdong Ziyunxuan Agricultural Development (herb sourcing firm controlled by Dashenlin co-controller Ke Jinlong); listed by Hurun with Ke Jinlong
profile: Wang Chunchan (王春婵) appears on Hurun lists jointly with Ke Jinlong, one of the three Ke brothers who founded and control Dashenlin Pharmaceutical (603233.SH), a Guangdong pharmacy chain that began in Maoming in the 1990s and listed in Shanghai in 2017. Dashenlin's 2026 filing names her legal rep of a Ke Jinlong-controlled Chinese herbal medicine sourcing company.
interesting_fact: Dashenlin grew from a single Maoming pharmacy into one of China's largest drugstore chains; its store count went from 32 in 2001 to 255 by 2006 after the Ke brothers studied Japanese chain-pharmacy management.
notes: Her exact relationship to Ke Jinlong (likely a spouse) is not confirmed in sources I found; role per Dashenlin related-party disclosure (https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2026-04/24/B384/zqB38424.pdf). Ke Jinlong has stepped back from Dashenlin and faces legal proceedings; avoid in outreach. IR email is Dashenlin board office, not hers.

name: Yoji Sato
current_role: Non-executive Director, Dynam Japan Holdings (HKEX: 6889); Chairman, Eurasia Foundation (from Asia)
profile: Yoji Sato (b. ~1946, Waseda commerce 1968) took over his father's pachinko business Sawa Shoji in 1970 aged 24 and built it into Dynam, Japan's largest pachinko hall operator, listing it in Hong Kong in 2012 as one of the first Japanese companies there. He moved from chairman/CEO to non-executive director in 2016; his vehicle SAC holds the controlling stake.
interesting_fact: Dynam listed on the Hong Kong exchange in 2012 because pachinko operators could not list in Tokyo; it was only the second Japanese issuer in Hong Kong after SBI Holdings.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking over the family firm he worked at supermarket chain Daiei because he was fascinated by the then-novel 'chain store theory', which he later applied to pachinko halls (suburban, low-cost formats, hiring new grads, forming a labour union).
notes: Age 80 per Dynam FY2025/26 annual report. Since 2009 he has chaired the One Asia / Eurasia Foundation (from Asia), which funds university courses on Asian community-building in many countries - a good warm angle. Foundation phone published on its site: +81-3-5615-5500.

name: Zeng Liqing
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Decent Capital (德迅投资); Tencent co-founder and lifetime honorary adviser
profile: Zeng Liqing (曾李青, b. 1970, Guangzhou) co-founded Tencent in 1998 as the third founder alongside Pony Ma and Tony Zhang, serving as COO 1999-2007 and running sales and marketing. Since leaving operations he has been an active angel/VC investor through Decent Capital, backing consumer internet, gaming and hard-tech start-ups.
interesting_fact: Decent Capital was an early backer of robot maker Unitree, investing about RMB4.6m across two rounds in 2019; its remaining stake was later valued at roughly RMB1.9bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tencent he was an engineer at Shenzhen Telecom's data bureau and drove what is described as the first broadband-wired residential compound in Shenzhen (and China) in the mid-1990s; he met Pony Ma through Ma's sister, a colleague at the bureau.
notes: Xidian University alumnus (telecoms). Decent Capital site is JS-rendered; no published email found. Best route is via Decent Capital or Chinese VC/startup events. Avoid mentioning his early QVOD investment.

name: Tang Xuejiao
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Manst Technology (曼恩斯特, SZSE: 301325); co-holder with GM/founder Peng Jianlin (彭建林)
profile: Tang Xuejiao (唐雪姣) chairs Shenzhen Manst Technology, founded in 2014 with Peng Jianlin (GM/CEO, Central South University graduate). Manst makes high-precision slot-die coating heads and coating lines for lithium-ion battery electrodes, plus hydrogen electrolysis, energy storage and semiconductor coating equipment; it listed on ChiNext in 2022/23.
interesting_fact: Manst says its slot-die coating heads broke foreign makers' monopoly in lithium battery electrode coating; it is now a national 'little giant' and Guangdong manufacturing single-champion with 260+ patents, and has expanded into water-electrolysis hydrogen.
notes: Input name_chinese (彭建林) is actually the co-holder Peng Jianlin; Tang Xuejiao is chairman per MarketScreener/Simply Wall St (https://simplywall.st/stocks/cn/capital-goods/szse-301325/shenzhen-manst-technology-shares/management). Strong energy-storage/hydrogen angle. Brand-department email is the best published media route.

name: Cherry Wang
current_role: Formosa Plastics heir; long-time executive in the Chang Gung Memorial Hospital system (current title not confirmed)
profile: Cherry Wang (王瑞慧) is the third daughter of Formosa Plastics founder Wang Yung-ching. A Columbia University psychology graduate, she rotated through ~18 Formosa units before joining Chang Gung's general management office in 1996, where she led hospital construction projects. Her wealth stems from inherited Formosa Plastics Group holdings.
interesting_fact: She led construction of the Chiayi, Yunlin and Xiamen Chang Gung hospitals; Xiamen Chang Gung was her father's first hospital in mainland China.
deep_cut_fact: While building Xiamen Chang Gung she visited the site more than 100 times, at first commuting almost weekly via the Kinmen 'mini three links' ferry, and she also ran the renovation of the Huayang Hotel in Luoyang.
notes: Very private; most coverage dates from 2007-2017. Avoid family/board disputes and her past marriage. No published personal or office contact found; Chang Gung/Formosa corporate channels are the only route.

name: Lin Rongbin
current_role: Founder, Fuzhou Sansheng (三盛) Group; controlling shareholder of Sansheng Holdings (Group) (HKEX: 2183) - current status not verified
profile: Lin Rongbin (林荣滨) is the Fujian entrepreneur who founded Fuzhou-based Sansheng Group, a property developer and investor. In 2017 he bought control of Hong Kong-listed Lifestyle Properties Development from Lau Luen-hung's Lifestyle International and renamed it Sansheng Holdings as a listed platform for mainland real estate.
interesting_fact: In April 2017 he paid HK$1.293bn (HK$5.18/share) for a 59.56% stake in Lifestyle Properties, the property spin-off of Hong Kong's SOGO owner Lifestyle International, which became Sansheng Holdings.
notes: Web-search budget ran out before full research; only Wikipedia was verified. Sansheng's website (sansheng.hk) was unreachable and no HKEX filings were found under 2183, so the listing may have changed. Chinese developers have been under stress since 2021, so frame outreach carefully. No published contacts found.

name: Yu Lanjun
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller (19.66%) of Tonghua Golden-Horse Pharmaceutical (通化金马, SZSE: 000766); deputy GM of Liaoning Lingyuan Gangda Group Industrial
profile: Yu Lanjun (于兰军), a Liaoning businessman, is deputy GM of Liaoning Lingyuan Gangda Group Industrial and runs Shenyang Jinhaoxin Trading and Shenyang Zhongtuan Technology. In 2022 he became the largest shareholder and actual controller of Jilin-based TCM drugmaker Tonghua Golden-Horse, where he holds 190m shares (19.66%); he holds no executive post there.
interesting_fact: He became Tonghua Golden-Horse's controller in 2022 when a Chengdu court awarded him 80m shares owed by the previous controller, Beijing Jinshang Alliance, which then formally agreed to his taking control.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews or biography found. Day-to-day leadership at Tonghua Golden-Horse is chairman/GM Zhang Yufu. Part of his stake is pledged. The IR email belongs to the company, not to him.
